statement: For every p in [0,1] on a countable connected bounded-degree graph, the two-point kernel T_p of Bernoulli bond percolation is positive semidefinite and its ell2 operator norm equals sup_F ||T_p^F||, with F finite connected free-boundary subgraphs and infinity allowed.
assumptions: Countable connected bounded-degree undirected simple graph
source: ATTEMPT.md L1; owner campaign proof reconstruction; operator background arXiv:1804.10191v3 Section 2
proof_or_counterexample: Cluster partition identity proves positivity; finite connecting paths and monotone exhaustion converge on finite-support nonnegative vectors; absolute values and polarization give both norm inequalities.

statement: Let G be an infinite connected bounded-degree Cayley graph with 0<p_c<1, alpha=||A_G||_2, and sup_F ||T_pc^F||<=M<infinity. Then p_u>=p_c+min{(1-p_c)/2,1/(2 alpha M)}>p_c.
assumptions: Arbitrary fixed finite symmetric generating set
Uniform critical finite-volume ell2 bound M

proof_or_counterexample: L2 bounds all finite T_q by 2M on the displayed interval; L1 bounds the full T_q. A unique infinite cluster would give T_q(x,y)>=theta(q)^2 by transitivity and FKG, contradicting quadratic forms on unit vectors supported on n distinct vertices.
remaining_gap: For the parent C0047 claim, prove sup_F ||T_pc^F||<infinity from nonamenability alone. This stronger input remains unproved.

statement: If rho denotes the normalized simple-random-walk spectral radius on a nonamenable d-regular Cayley graph, the inequality p_c<1/rho is automatic and is not the difficult input of the elementary two-point path bound. That bound instead supplies the sufficient condition p_c d rho<1, with alpha=||A||_2=d rho; it is not a necessary condition for p_c<p_u.
assumptions: Kesten's rho<1 characterization for this setting

statement: Let G be an infinite connected simple d-regular graph, d>=3, b=d-1, alpha=||A||_2, and beta=sqrt(b) when alpha<=2sqrt(b), otherwise beta=(alpha+sqrt(alpha^2-4b))/2. For Bernoulli bond percolation and 0<=p<1/beta, ||T_p||_2<=(1-p^2)/(1+b p^2-alpha p). For Cayley graphs, p_c beta<1 is a sufficient input to L3.
assumptions: Infinite connected simple d-regular graph, d>=3
Fixed generating set in the Cayley corollary
source: NONBACKTRACKING_LEMMA.md; owner campaign reconstruction of the standard nonbacktracking bound
proof_or_counterexample: Count nonbacktracking walks B_n, prove B_2=A^2-dI and B_n=A B_n-1-(d-1)B_n-2 for n>=3. Spectral recurrence roots have modulus at most beta, giving norm convergence of sum p^n B_n. Its resolvent is (1-p^2)(I-pA+b p^2 I)^-1. Union bound only on edge-distinct simple paths, then increase counts to B_n.
remaining_gap: Nonamenability alone is not shown to imply p_c beta<1; the parent route's uniform critical norm input remains unproved.
review_status: author proof, not independently checked; novelty not claimed

statement: For the infinite d-regular tree, d>=3 and b=d-1, Bernoulli bond percolation has p_c=1/b and ||T_pc||_2=(1-b^-2)/(1-b^-1/2)^2<infinity. Thus L3 proves a positive conditional margin on the entire tree family. The coarse p_c||A||<1 test holds only for d>=6, while the nonbacktracking sufficient test holds for every d>=3.
proof_or_counterexample: Simple tree paths make the nonbacktracking kernel exact. Orienting toward an end proves ||A||<=2sqrt(b), and truncated radial vectors prove equality. The resolvent then has the displayed exact critical norm; p_c=1/b follows from branching-process survival.
remaining_gap: No gap within the tree special case; no assertion for other nonamenable graphs.
review_status: author proof, not independently checked; known tree case, no novelty claim

statement: For Bernoulli bond percolation on Cay(C_3*C_2,{a,a^-1,s}), a of order 3 and s of order 2, the graph is 3-regular nonamenable and satisfies p_c>3/5, ||A||_2>=2+2sqrt(2)/3, and beta=(||A||_2+sqrt(||A||_2^2-8))/2>5/3. Therefore p_c beta>1 and nonamenability does not universally imply L4's sufficient input p_c beta<1. This graph has p_u=1, so it is not a counterexample to C0047.
assumptions: Fixed standard simple Cayley graph of C_3*C_2
source: NB_ROUTE_OBSTRUCTION.md; owner campaign route obstruction; w559's independent triangle-family lane noted, not used as a proof audit
proof_or_counterexample: Contract triangles to T_3. A forest boundary count proves h_E>=1/3. Disjoint block exploration has mean 2p(p+p^2-p^3), which equals 558/625 at p=3/5. Constant-on-triangle test vectors give the adjacency lower bound. Since z+2/z at z=5/3 is 43/15<2+2sqrt(2)/3, beta>5/3. A closed bridge separates independently surviving half-tree clusters for p>p_c, giving p_u=1.
